clue.text: Puzzles about what might move the public

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
buses are public transport, vehicles that carry people around

explanation.surface: Riddles concerning whatever might stir up popular feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move the public' reads as stirring emotions, but it means carrying people from place to place.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture puzzles made of letters and symbols are a kind of puzzle, so this is a specific example of the general word.

clue.text: Centre in Zurich checks fastenings

indicators.note: centre in picks out the middle letters of the following word

parts.note: vets means checks or examines thoroughly

explanation.surface: A central Zurich bank checks fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: metal pins hammered flat to hold plates together are a type of fastening.

clue.text: Some part of crab is questionable for soup

indicators.note: some part of means the answer is a run of letters within these words

explanation.surface: Is a bit of crab dubious to put in soup?
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rich, creamy soup made from shellfish such as lobster or crab.

clue.text: View pint, not sad to get tipsy

indicators.note: someone tipsy is unsteady, so the letters of pint, not and sad are mixed up

explanation.surface: Drinking a pint not to drown sorrow but to get merry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a point of view or opinion on a matter is one's view.

clue.text: Not drunk provided beer, half-empty

parts.note: so can mean provided that, as in 'so you agree'

indicators.note: half-empty means the pair of identical middle letters is drained to just one, half the contents

explanation.surface: Staying dry, as long as the beer glass is half drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-empty' leaves one of the two Es in BEER, giving BER, rather than keeping half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym phrasing: someone who has not been drinking alcohol is clear-headed.

clue.text: Held cap with sled out of control

indicators.note: a sled out of control careers about, so the letters of cap and sled are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clutching their hat while a sledge runs away with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' rearranges the letters of CAP and SLED together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have gripped something tightly in the hand is to have held it.

clue.text: Cruel cops sabotaged cell

indicators.note: sabotaged means wrecked, so the letters of cruel and cops are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brutal police wrecked a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' looks like a prison room but is a blood cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a red or white cell floating in the blood is a type of cell in the body.

clue.text: Excuse me, answer what upset Mike

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so these letters run the other way

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what?
Mike is the radio code word for the letter M

explanation.surface: A polite cough before answering what upset Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EH plus M into HEM, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection: a small cough said to attract attention politely, much as one might say pardon.

clue.text: Harassed professional, very fine editor

parts.note: pro is short for professional
OK means fine or acceptable

explanation.surface: A professional, a very good editor, was hassled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have needled or goaded someone into reacting is to have harassed them.

clue.text: Wearisome taking food around soldiers

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: dining is taking a meal
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Eating while surrounded by troops is tiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: exhausting, energy-sapping work is described as wearisome.

clue.text: Scene five is at back

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: back tells us the word at is turned round to run the other way

explanation.surface: Something numbered five appears at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the turnaround signal, not a position: TA ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a broad view of landscape is a scene laid out before you.

clue.text: Unopened package carried by toff around a Spanish city

indicators.note: something carried by a person is held within them, so one piece goes inside another
around signals that the word for toff is turned the other way

parts.note: a nob is a British slang word for a toff, an upper-class person

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter of the word for package is removed

parts.note: a parcel is a wrapped package

explanation.surface: A posh traveller lugs a parcel round a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toff' is British slang for an upper-class person, here NOB; 'Unopened' removes the first letter, and 'around' turns NOB to BON.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the Catalan capital on Spain's Mediterranean coast, a major city of Spain.

clue.text: Welcoming North; unfortunately South rude and noisy

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so one letter goes inside the rest
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of South and rude are jumbled

explanation.surface: A northern guest is welcomed, but a rude, loud southerner spoils it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' gives THUDEROUS, and 'Welcoming' takes N into it; South is fodder, not a compass abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something extremely loud, like rumbling thunder, is noisy.

clue.text: Couple jogging no good at all

indicators.note: G stands for good, and having none at all of it means every G in jogging is removed

explanation.surface: A pair who find going for a run completely useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good at all' removes all three Gs from JOGGING, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to couple two things is to link or connect them together.

clue.text: Amateur boxing second is natural

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: untrained means lacking professional training, as an amateur does

explanation.surface: An amateur boxer's second has a natural talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport, but it means putting S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unforced, effortless behaviour that is not laboured is natural.

clue.text: Running business is becoming worry

parts.note: going, as in going grey, means becoming
concern is another word for worry

explanation.surface: Keeping a company going is turning into a source of anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like a verb, but 'Running business' is the definition: a firm in operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a firm that is trading and expected to continue operating is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Without restrictions of time, lad from south calls

indicators.note: in a down clue, from south means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a son is a lad
rings means telephones or calls

explanation.surface: A boy from the south phones without any time limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from south' reads SON upwards as NOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an offer with no conditions or catches attached is given freely.

clue.text: African gent I pay is dodgy

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters of gent I pay are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man from Africa whom I'm paying is shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a person from the Nile country is one nationality from that continent.

clue.text: County club needing several runs to lead

parts.note: some means several
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a set is a group of people, like a club

explanation.surface: A county cricket club needs runs to go top.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in south-west England with a cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is one of the counties of England, in the south-west.

clue.text: Layers beneath kippers of crushed leaves

parts.note: ground, as in ground coffee, means crushed into small pieces
sheets of paper are also called leaves

explanation.surface: Smoked fish layered on a bed of crushed leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kippers' are not smoked herrings but people kipping, British slang for sleeping; campers lay these waterproof sheets under them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: campers sleep on waterproof sheets laid under them on the tent floor, so these lie beneath sleepers.

clue.text: Oddly glitzy male with very big gadgets

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: A flashy man with huge devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: small mechanical devices or contraptions are informally called gadgets.

clue.text: Daughter wearing odd welly in improper way

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wear the D, holding it inside like a garment
odd means strange, so the letters of welly are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl in a mismatched wellington boot looks unseemly.
explanation.walkthrough: A welly is British for a wellington, a rubber boot. 'odd' rearranges WELLY into LEWLY, and 'wearing' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: behaving crudely or obscenely is acting in an indecent, improper manner.

clue.text: Relieved exclamation not many heard

indicators.note: heard signals that the word sounds like another word when spoken

parts.note: few means not many

explanation.surface: Only a handful of people caught someone's sigh of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection: people say this word on escaping danger or finishing a strain, expressing relief.

clue.text: Ignore American wearing his beard stupidly

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wear the American abbreviation, holding it inside like clothing
stupidly suggests something done wrongly, so the letters of his and beard are rearranged

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: An American man sporting a ridiculous beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' gives BRHASIDE, and 'wearing' takes the American abbreviation into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to dismiss or disregard something without considering it is to sweep it away from you.

clue.text: Cook's note to replace second bit of Spam

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped out for the note
second bit of points at the letter in second place of the word

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A chef's memo about swapping something in a tin of luncheon meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second bit of Spam' is P; 'to replace' puts TE in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: to cook food over boiling water is one method of cooking.

clue.text: Chimney went skyward, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: flew means went up into the sky

explanation.surface: Smoke rose up through the chimney, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Part for whole: the duct inside a chimney that carries smoke away.

clue.text: Rudeness in church eating fish head in nave

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes another into itself

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour in church: someone eating a fish head in the nave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' splits the IN-plus-church pair, with the fish and N ('head in nave') between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: disrespectful, cheeky behaviour towards others is a form of rudeness.

clue.text: Called retired mother in home

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole assembly runs backwards
in places the word for mother inside the word for home

parts.note: a den is a home or lair
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A retired mother at home was summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes DEMAN first, and 'retired' then reads the whole of it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have given someone or something a name is to have called it that.

clue.text: Rabbits two times caught in activated snare

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so these letters go inside the rest
an activated snare springs into a new shape, so its letters are rearranged
two calls for the letter to be used twice over

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for times, as in multiplication

explanation.surface: Rabbits twice trapped by a sprung snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activated' gives NAERS for 'caught in' to hold. 'Rabbits' is a verb here, British slang for chatters.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to rabbit on is to talk at length about trivial things, which is chattering.

clue.text: Way, way, way at the back showing shyness

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
St is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way

indicators.note: at the back picks out the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone hanging back at the rear of the road, showing bashfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is used three ways: MODE, ST and the last letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reluctance to show off or draw attention to oneself is a kind of bashfulness.
